summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of chronic pancreatitis, recurrent cellulitis, venous stasis ulcers, and multiple comorbidities was admitted for worsening left leg cellulitis that progressed despite prior antibiotic treatment. She presented with erythema, pain, cracked skin, and discharge from chronic ulcers, along with low-grade fevers and chills. IV vancomycin and ciprofloxacin were started, and wound culture grew methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus. Imaging showed soft tissue edema without abscess or deep vein thrombosis, and vascular studies revealed normal arterial flow. Due to persistent infection and poor response, she was transitioned to oral linezolid. A mild drug rash that developed after prior doxycycline use resolved spontaneously. She was discharged home on a four-week course of linezolid, iron supplementation, and oxycodone for pain, with instructions to stop tramadol due to interaction risk, discontinue compression devices until skin healing, and follow up for wound care, infectious disease, and colonoscopy for iron deficiency anemia.
